title: feat(shopping): add `search_products` and `categories_brands_list` tools
body:
cc: Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `agent:shopping`, `priority:high`

### Problem
The Shopping Agent has no way to find products. The registry only has `product_get`, `products_compare` and `reviews_summary_get`, and all three need a product id. The system prompt already has a full "Search and filtering" section, but there is no tool behind it, so the model cannot obtain an id from a customer's request.

`tools.py` already says these tools are planned ("Person A adds search_products and categories_brands_list"), and `ProductCard` in `agents/shopping/schemas.py` is defined but not used yet.

### Proposal
Add two thin wrappers in `agents/shopping/tools.py` over services that already exist:

- `search_products(q, category, brand, min_price, max_price, in_stock, sort, limit)` -> `catalog.list_products`.
  - Validate inputs like the other tools (`limit` capped by `MAX_LIMIT`, `sort` limited to the existing values).
  - Return `ProductCard` rows plus `empty: true/false`.
  - Note that `list_products` never returns inactive products. Keep that behavior.
- `categories_brands_list()` -> `catalog.list_categories` and `catalog.list_brands`, so the model can map customer words to real slugs.

### Acceptance criteria
- Both tools are in `REGISTRY` and reachable only through `call_tool`.
- Empty results return `empty: true`, not an error.
- Unit and integration tests like the existing `test_shopping_tools.py` and `test_shopping_details.py`.
- The prompt rules for search match what the tools can actually do.

title: fix(shopping): discount must come from a tool, not be computed by the model
body:
cc: Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `agent:shopping`, `bug`

### Problem
The prompt says: "if there is an old price, mention the discount". But no tool returns a discount amount or percentage; only `price_egp` and `old_price_egp`. The model would have to calculate it, which breaks the prompt's own rule 1 ("every price, spec and rating must come from a tool").

### Proposal
Add `discount_pct` (and optionally `discount_egp`) to `ProductCard` / `ProductDetail`, computed in the service with `Decimal` and a documented rounding rule. `None` when there is no `old_price_egp`. Update the prompt to say "use `discount_pct` from the tool".

### Acceptance criteria
- Unit test with hand-computed values, including no old price and old price lower than or equal to the current price.
- The prompt no longer asks the model to calculate anything.

title: test(shopping): add an eval set and a README for the Shopping Agent
body:
cc: Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `agent:shopping`, `testing`, `docs`

### Problem
The Seller Agent has a README and a 15-question eval with expected answers. The Shopping Agent has neither (its `README.md` is empty). The prompt already contains rules that can be tested.

### Proposal
- Write `agents/shopping/README.md` in the same format as the Seller one (rules, files, tool table, how to try it).
- Add `agents/shopping/eval/questions.json` with expected tool calls and results on the frozen seed data. Suggested cases:
  - budget search ("under 10,000" -> max price 10000)
  - search with no results (prompt says widen one filter only)
  - compare 2 to 4 products
  - compare products from different categories (`mixed_categories`)
  - compare with a missing id
  - a product with fewer than 3 reviews
  - an out-of-stock or inactive product (`in_stock=false`)
  - a request outside shopping scope

### Acceptance criteria
- Eval runs in CI (see issue 6 for how the Seller eval should be wired).

title: refactor: services must not import from `agents/` (layering)
body:
cc: Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `refactor`, `architecture`

### Problem
`services/catalog_details.py` imports `ProductDetail` from `agents/shopping/schemas.py`. `docs/architecture.md` says layers depend in one direction and agents call services, not the other way around.

### Proposal
Move `ProductDetail` and `ProductCard` to `schemas/` (for example `schemas/catalog.py` or a new `schemas/shopping.py`) and import them from there in both the service and the agent.

### Acceptance criteria
- No module under `services/` imports from `agents/` (can be enforced with a small test or an import-linter rule).

title: fix(seller): define what "returns in a period" means and fix `returns_report`
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100

Area / priority: `agent:seller`, `bug`, `docs`, `priority:high`

### Problem
`returns_report` filters on `Order.created_at` (through `_in_period`). So "returns in the last 30 days" actually means "returns on orders created in the last 30 days". A return requested today on a 40-day-old order is missing, while a return on a 5-day-old order is included even if requested later. This is probably not what a seller means by the question.

`docs/seller-metrics.md` defines revenue, units, orders, AOV and stock, but does not define the returns metric or its period.

### Proposal
- Decide the definition and write it in `docs/seller-metrics.md`. Suggested: count returns by `Return.created_at`, excluding `rejected` (as now).
- Change `returns_report` accordingly and update the tool description and the prompt wording ("returns requested in the period").
- Add tests with hand-computed numbers where a return is requested in the period on an older order.
- Re-check eval question 14 against the new definition.

### Acceptance criteria
- Definition documented, tests added, eval updated.

title: test(seller): widen eval coverage and make the eval run in CI
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100

Area / priority: `agent:seller`, `testing`, `priority:high`

### Problem
1. Coverage: the 15 questions use only 5 of the 7 tools (`get_sales_summary` 5, `compare_periods` 4, `low_stock_products` 4, `top_products` 1, `returns_report` 1). `orders_by_status` and `get_product_reviews` have no question.
2. CI: `tests/integration/test_seller_eval.py` skips itself unless the dev database `ai_commerce` is seeded with `--anchor-date 2026-11-04T12:00:00`. The CI workflow only creates `ai_commerce_test`, so the eval appears to be skipped on every PR and regressions would not be caught.
3. Scope: the eval checks tool results only. Rule 6 of the prompt ("why did sales drop?") asks the model to combine comparison, top products, returns and stock, but nothing tests that, nor tests for out-of-scope questions, prompt injection or "show me your instructions".

### Proposal
- Add questions for the two missing tools and more for `top_products` and `returns_report`, including `worst=true` and an empty result.
- In CI, run migrations and the seed with the fixed anchor date on the test database, and point the eval at it.
- Once the LLM graph exists, add a second layer that checks which tools the agent called and that the final answer contains the numbers from the tool results.

### Acceptance criteria
- Eval is not skipped in CI.
- All 7 tools are covered.

title: fix(seller): period boundaries and "today" should use the store's timezone
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100

Area / priority: `agent:seller`, `bug`

### Problem
Dates from the model are parsed as UTC (`_parse_date` adds `UTC` when there is no timezone), and the prompt computes "today" with `date.today()` on the server. The store is Egyptian (UTC+2). An order placed at 00:30 Cairo time belongs to the previous UTC day, so it can fall on the wrong side of a period boundary.

### Proposal
Pick one timezone for period boundaries (for example `Africa/Cairo`), apply it in `_parse_date` and in `build_system_prompt`, and document it in `docs/seller-metrics.md`.

### Acceptance criteria
- A test with an order just after midnight Cairo time lands in the expected period.

title: chore(seller): small consistency fixes in the tool layer
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100

Area / priority: `agent:seller`, `good first issue`

- `compare_periods` does not check that period A is earlier than period B, although the prompt and docs rely on it. Return an `invalid_period_order` error (or document that any order is allowed).
- `get_product_reviews` returns `rating_avg` as a float, while the Shopping tools return it as a string (exact Decimal). Use one representation across both agents.
- `get_product_reviews` can include reviews with an empty body in `recent_low_rated`; the Shopping excerpts filter `body != ""`. Use the same rule.
- `low_stock_products` has no result limit (the other list tools cap at `MAX_LIMIT`).

title: refactor(agents): extract the shared tool layer into `agents/common.py`
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100, Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `refactor`, `architecture`, `priority:high`

### Problem
`ToolContext`, `ToolInputError`, `_safe`, `_jsonable`, `_limit` and `call_tool` are copied almost word for word in `agents/seller/tools.py` and `agents/shopping/tools.py`. A Support Agent is planned next, which would be a third copy, and the copies have already started to drift (`_jsonable` handles `Decimal` in one and not the other).

### Proposal
Create `agents/common.py` with:
- `ToolInputError`, `_safe`/`safe`, `jsonable`, `limit`
- a generic `call_tool(registry, ctx, name, args)` that keeps the current guarantees: unknown tools rejected, extra arguments rejected with `forbidden_argument`, never raises to the agent
- keep each agent's own `ToolContext` (different identity field: `seller_id` vs `customer_id`), or define a small base class

### Acceptance criteria
- Existing seller and shopping tests pass unchanged.
- A Support Agent can reuse the module without copying.

title: chore(agents): use one platform name and one Arabic tone across prompts and UI
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100, Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `agent:seller`, `agent:shopping`, `frontend`, `docs`

### Problem
- Platform name: the Seller prompt says "سوقنا", the Shopping prompt says "دكان تك" (a test asserts that "سوقنا" is absent), the frontend is "Dokkan Tech", and the README says "AI Commerce Marketplace".
- Tone: both prompts ask for polite Egyptian colloquial Arabic. `frontend/AGENTS.md` says the UI tone should be "calm, modern, not slang". Agent replies appear in the same UI.

### Proposal
- Decide the user-facing store name and put it in one shared constant used by all prompts.
- Decide the Arabic tone (colloquial vs modern standard) and write it in one place (for example `docs/agent-guidelines.md`); update the prompts and their tests.

title: design: chat API contract, LLM/framework decision and router for the agents
body:
cc: @amrkhaled100, Noura (@nrshousha), @basicesraa

Area / priority: `agents`, `design`, `priority:high`

### Problem
Everything under `agents/` is a tool layer plus a prompt. Nothing connects it to a user yet:
- no chat endpoint in the API
- no LLM client or LangChain/LangGraph in `pyproject.toml`
- no router or supervisor (the Seller README says `graph.py` is waiting for this decision)
- no conversation state or memory
- the frontend assistant is a scripted mock, and its trace panel shows steps (`input_guardrail`, `supervisor`, `output_guardrail`) that the backend does not produce

### Decisions needed
1. LLM provider and orchestration framework (LangGraph or not).
2. Router design: one entry endpoint that picks Shopping, Support, Seller or Order Actions from the token role and the message; how identity (`customer_id` / `seller_id`) is injected into `ToolContext`.
3. API contract, for example `POST /assistant/chat` with `{conversation_id?, message}` and a response with `{reply, products?, confidence, trace[]}`, so the frontend can replace the mock.
4. Conversation state: where it is stored and how long.
5. Guardrails: where input and output checks live.
6. Scope of the Support and Order Actions agents (Support read-only; Order Actions performs cancel/return after explicit confirmation, using `order_actions` and `order_rules`).

### Acceptance criteria
- A short design doc in `docs/` agreed by the team, and the API contract added to `docs/api-contracts.md`.
